answers.answer: An HTTP cache retains response bodies plus metadata such as status and headers for reuse. The browser private cache serves one user agent; a CDN runs shared caches at edge servers near users; origin is the server responsible for the resource. A hit finds a suitable stored response; a miss has none usable. Empty: browser → CDN → origin, then response origin → CDN → browser, stored at each layer only if policy permits. A browser hit avoids the network. Another browser missing locally can hit the CDN and avoid origin. Caches store HTTP responses, not replicated database records; origin may consult a database but hits need not reach either. At the specified CDN, request hit ratio = hits / requests = 800/1000 = 80%; origin receives 200 requests under the stated assumptions. Browser hits never reach that denominator; response sizes differ so this is not bytes saved. Validation, background refresh, additional layers and application/database work require separate measurement in real traffic. Repeated public assets can reduce latency through nearby responses, origin requests/load and transfer. CDN requests/transfer can cost money, while keys, invalidation and monitoring cost operational effort. For low-traffic mostly private or rarely reused Notes responses, omit shared caching when measured reuse, latency and total cost do not justify it; keep privacy intact.

evidence.quote: A browser hit avoids the network request. After a browser miss, a CDN hit avoids origin.
The ratio is 800 / 1,000 = 80%.
Compare reuse, latency and total cost.

answers.answer: Cache-Control carries response caching directives. public permits shared caching subject to other rules; max-age=60 gives 60 seconds freshness; s-maxage=300 overrides the lifetime only for shared caches. Fresh means young enough for reuse without validation under policy; stale means the freshness limit has been reached, not necessarily that the body is deleted. Age estimates seconds since origin generation or successful validation, including time in caches. At Age 90 the browser is stale by 30 seconds (60−90 = −30, zero freshness remaining); the CDN remains fresh for 210 seconds (300−90). Delivery does not reset the lifetime, and freshness does not prove unchanged origin content. A representation is the returned form of a resource. Revalidation checks whether the stored representation remains usable. ETag is an opaque representation validator preserved without interpretation. The stale CDN sends a conditional GET to origin with If-None-Match: "v1", requesting a body only if the selected representation no longer matches. Unchanged: origin returns 304 Not Modified without a replacement body; CDN updates applicable metadata, including freshness, and serves its retained v1 body for the ordinary browser GET. Changed: origin returns 200 with the new body and ETag "v2"; CDN serves the new body and replaces its stored representation if policy allows. An ETag does not push changes elsewhere. Validation still requires the origin round trip and may invoke application logic or database queries; 304 saves body transfer across that hop.

evidence.quote: The CDN has 300 − 90 = 210 seconds of freshness left.
Freshness is permission to reuse, not proof that origin content is unchanged.
The CDN updates applicable stored metadata, including freshness information, and uses its retained body to answer the browser's ordinary GET.
Origin was still contacted and may run application logic or query a database to decide whether the representation changed.

answers.answer: Cookies are browser-held state; Set-Cookie asks the browser to store it, and Cookie sends it back. Authorization is a request header carrying credentials. Authentication establishes identity; authorization checks permission to access a resource. For the public page use unqualified Cache-Control: no-cache: storage is allowed but successful validation is required before every reuse. For a private note where browser storage is acceptable use private: shared-cache storage is forbidden, browser storage remains allowed and validation on every use is not required by private alone; other directives still apply. For the sensitive note use no-store to instruct HTTP caches not to store it. no-store cannot erase already delivered copies or replace permission checks. Cookie/Set-Cookie neither automatically separate entries by user nor universally prevent caching; Authorization requests have special shared-cache restrictions but response policies can permit reuse, so authentication is no universal bypass guarantee. Reusing one user’s response for another leaks private data. Keep authorization at origin and verify explicit private/no-store policies together with actual CDN rules prevent shared storage and reuse for private routes. Test across different users and do not make personalized responses public to increase hit rate.

evidence.quote: Authentication establishes identity; authorization checks permission to access a resource.
no-cache means validate; no-store means do not store; private excludes shared caches.
Cookie and Set-Cookie do not automatically create per-user cache entries or universally prevent caching.
For private routes, verify that explicit private/no-store policies and actual CDN rules prevent shared storage and reuse.

answers.answer: A cache key identifies which stored response can satisfy a request. A representation variant is a different returned form of the same resource. HTTP caching uses method and target URL plus selected request headers to distinguish variants. Keep ?format=pdf and ?format=html distinct, and distinguish Accept-Language en from fr. Vary names request headers whose values must match for response reuse; Vary: Accept-Language separates language variants when supported and honored. If the CDN ignores query parameters, verify and correct the actual key settings so meaningful format values remain distinct; also verify language survives matching, or bypass caching until both work. Dropping format can serve HTML for a PDF request; dropping language can reuse the wrong language. Irrelevant tracking parameters create extra entries and fewer hits; exclude only after confirming they do not change the response. Vary does not change the URL, grant permission, or override private/no-store, so it never authorizes sharing private notes.

evidence.quote: A cache key identifies which stored response can satisfy a request.
Vary: Accept-Language tells a cache that this request header's value must match for reuse.
verify that both format and language survive the actual matching rules, or bypass caching until they do.
Vary does not change the URL, grant permission or override private/no-store.

answers.answer: A versioned asset URL changes when its bytes change. Publish app.v2.js rather than overwriting app.v1.js; each immutable asset URL keeps unchanged bytes and can use long caching. Update the referring page to request v2, while recognizing an old cached page can still request v1. A mutable published page retaining its URL needs freshness/revalidation chosen for tolerated update delay, such as short freshness or validation on every reuse. A database update does not rewrite stored HTTP responses. A CDN purge removes or invalidates targeted CDN entries according to provider behavior. Check coverage of relevant URLs, variants and CDN layers, propagation and completion rather than assuming simultaneous replacement. Purging does not evict fresh browser copies or erase downloads. Unpublishing can stop future origin access and trigger purges, but already delivered public content cannot be instantly revoked; choose lifetimes with that limit before publication.

evidence.quote: Update the referring page to request v2; an old cached page can still ask for v1.
A database edit does not rewrite stored HTTP responses.
Verify coverage of the relevant URLs, variants and CDN cache layers, plus propagation and completion behavior.
Purging CDN entries does not evict fresh browser copies or erase downloaded content.

answers.answer: stale-while-revalidate permits bounded stale reuse while attempting background validation to hide validation latency. stale-if-error permits bounded stale fallback for eligible errors such as origin failure. These are optional permissions, not promises of freshness or availability. max-age=60 gives freshness for 60 seconds; both stale allowances start at expiry. At age 75 the copy is 15 seconds stale, within the 30-second stale-while-revalidate allowance through age 90: serve it while attempting background validation. At age 150 it is 90 seconds stale; with an eligible error it falls within stale-if-error’s 120 seconds after expiry, through age 180, so fallback is permitted. At age 200 it is 140 seconds stale and neither extension authorizes reuse. A cold cache has no copy to fall back to; expired allowances can expose failure. Verify support and policy, and do not override private/no-store. Private-data correctness and urgent removal may prohibit stale reuse despite improved public-help availability. No gaps identified for the supplied questions.

evidence.quote: The response is fresh for 60 seconds; stale windows start when freshness expires.
At age 200 neither extension still permits stale reuse.
A cold cache has no response to fall back to, and exhausted allowances can expose the failure.
Private-data correctness or urgent removal may forbid stale reuse even when it improves public-help availability.
